races.name: Cappawhite Civil Engineering 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Balance Of Trade
runners_data.note: Has form on Good ground and places in the field but is a genuine hold-up type who will be furthest from the action in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to reel in the front-runner; Alex Harvey partnership with Paul Mulligan (no runners in 14 days) suggests no strong stable confidence, and sim-going form is limited to zero wins from five runs.

runners_data.name: Boston Benjamin
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy for Gordon Elliott — the stable is firing (9/82 in 14 days) and this horse won over 7f on Standard and showed flat speed; now asked to settle over hurdles at 2m½f from a 74-day break but is a natural prominent racer who could track Minella Rockett and deliver a late challenge with top jockey assistance.

runners_data.name: Connor Of Mali
runners_data.note: Returns from a huge 266-day absence and has only one career start to reference (10th on Good); Luke Burke Ott (7) rides and the horse carries a fades-in-finish flag — its true preference is to come from off the pace, but with so many hold-up horses in this field, that rear position may not be available, and the layoff makes fitness a real question.

runners_data.name: Divelment
runners_data.note: Has placed twice over 10f on Standard and was active 34 days ago for William Durkan; at heart this horse wants to be ridden quietly and delivered late, but the abundance of hold-up runners means Patrick O'Brien (5) may find it sitting in midfield by default rather than choice — modest flat form on Good is an upgrade concern for hurdling.

runners_data.name: Minella Rockett
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner; Daniel King for John Nallen can dictate an uncontested lead and has the most straightforward tactical assignment in the race — showed a placed effort on Good going over 8f and the step to 2m½f over hurdles is the test, but the free ride in front compensates for the style-fit caveat flagged in the data.

runners_data.name: Nicky Larson
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan (3/14 in 14 days) sends out a horse that was second on Good and has placed on similar ground; Sean O'Keeffe rides and the horse's true nature is hold-up but the flat profile over 7-8f suggests enough tactical speed to sit closer than its label implies — one of the more likely of the redistributed runners to actually secure a forward berth.

runners_data.name: Notahairoutofplace
runners_data.note: Only one career run (14th over 12f on Good) and carries both a finish-fade flag and a 20-day turnaround; Calum Hogan (5) has limited support from R K Watson (0/2 in 14 days) and the evidence base for this horse hurdling is almost non-existent — hard to make a case.

runners_data.name: Swinging The World
runners_data.note: Consistently finishes well down the field on both Good and Soft going, carrying a fades-in-finish flag in almost every start; Danny Gilligan for Denise Foster (1/3 in 14 days) and the 31-day gap since last run adds no particular edge — the form profile does not encourage optimism in a race already tilted away from hold-up types.

runners_data.name: Words Unspoken
runners_data.note: Completely unknown quantity — no form, unknown style, unknown going preference, listed as a first-time hurdler with Phillip Enright for S Curling (no recent runners flagged); the wildcard of the field and impossible to assess, though a clean round of jumping on Good ground could make it competitive if the others disappoint.

runners_data.name: Sofi's Gift
runners_data.note: Josh Williamson (5) for Ciaran Murphy (2/16 in 14 days) and the horse has never finished better than 7th in four runs, all on Good or Soft; the 20-day turnaround is fresh enough but there is no form peak to point to, and 147lbs is the lightest weight in the field — a marginal weight edge that barely offsets the absence of any placed form.

races.paceDynamic: Minella Rockett is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to dispute the lead, Daniel King can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m½f trip on Good ground. The field is heavily weighted toward hold-up types — Balance Of Trade, Connor Of Mali, Divelment, Nicky Larson, Notahairoutofplace, Swinging The World and Sofi's Gift all want to come from off the pace — meaning the pace is almost certain to be modest and the race will compress into a tight unit through the middle stages before quickening home. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can honestly place at the rear; of those redistributed to midfield, Nicky Larson and Divelment are most likely to actually secure a forward position given their flat form profiles and jockey intent, while the others will be further back than ideal. This race shape — a lone front-runner controlling a gentle pace with a large hold-up pack grinding into it — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or in a handy midfield position and quicken off the home turn, rather than true deep closers who need a strong pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Minella Rockett Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Minella Rockett jumps well and settles into an uncontested lead, setting a moderate tempo that keeps the hold-up pack strung out.
scenarios.body: If Minella Rockett jumps well and settles into an uncontested lead, setting a moderate tempo that keeps the hold-up pack strung out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Minella Rockett sets only a crawl and a prominent tracker moves ominously into contention from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: If Minella Rockett sets only a crawl and a prominent tracker moves ominously into contention from the second-last hurdle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the leaders empty out from the second-last, allowing a strong-finishing closer to pick them off.
scenarios.body: If the pace is faster than expected and the leaders empty out from the second-last, allowing a strong-finishing closer to pick them off.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Multiple Errors/Falls
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors disrupt the front two and reshuffle the order, opening the door for an unconsidered runner.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors disrupt the front two and reshuffle the order, opening the door for an unconsidered runner.

watchPoints.text: Minella Rockett jumping — if Daniel King's front-runner makes a significant error at any of the early hurdles, the entire race shape collapses and the tactical read is void.
Boston Benjamin's stamina for 2m½f is unproven given all his flat form is over 7-8f; Jack Kennedy may need to ease him into it but if he travels too kindly he is a serious threat to the leader late.

The cluster of hold-up horses — Balance Of Trade, Divelment, Nicky Larson, Connor Of Mali — will all be trying to find the same ground racing off the home turn; watch for a traffic problem or interference as they converge on limited room.
Connor Of Mali returning from 266 days off is a significant fitness unknown — if it shows any early signs of racing freely or jumping poorly, discount it entirely despite the nominal potential.
Words Unspoken is a total unknown and Phillip Enright is capable of stealing ground on a loose-jumping debutant hurdler — monitor the early markets for any move that suggests stable confidence.

races.name: Cappawhite Civil Engineering Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Tuche De Houelle
runners_data.note: Lightly raced French import, off 412 days, and trainer A Chaille-Chaille & F Pamart have no recent UK/IRE form (T14: 0/16); the unknown quantity tag is real and the lengthy absence makes fitness a serious question mark — treat as a wildcard rather than a factor.|

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a genuine Good-ground win at 17f on his most recent start (1/17f/GOO); Paddy Hanlon (5) claims 5lb and trainer Hanlon's stable is running at 2/26 over 14 days — watch for a late run if the pace is strong enough to create a gap.|

runners_data.name: Youlita
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner and sole pace-setter, C Byrnes yard in good form (3/15 T14), latest win on Good (1/19f/GOO) and Sim-going record decent (4/8, 1W3P); STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) is less relevant here as she is expected to lead naturally, though she may prove vulnerable if tracked closely by Good-ground prominent types.|

runners_data.name: Bop Wont Stop
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a modest form profile (sim-going: 0W0P from 6 runs) and recent starts have yielded a 9th and 4th on Good; nothing in his record suggests he can overcome this field from off the pace and the form string is uninspiring.|

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy in the saddle for Gordon Elliott (T14: 9/65) is a strong combination; prominent style suits this race shape, with two seconds on Good ground including a 2/17f/GOO and a 2/18f/SOF — the tongue-tie (hg:h) is noted and he maps neatly to track Youlita.|

runners_data.name: Harpy Eagle
runners_data.note: Apprentice Paddy Cody (7) claims 7lb and trainer R P Cody has a quiet book (T14: 0/2); prominent style fits the anticipated shape, placed twice on Good (2/16f/GOO, 4/19f/HEA), and 122 days off may mean he needs the run but Good ground is fine.|

runners_data.name: Silly Mongoose
runners_data.note: Recent winner on Good at Limerick (1/16f/GOO) is the standout credential; hold-up horse with tongue-tie, trainer Foley sent him out 17 days ago and the horse is clearly fit — if this develops into a strong-run race he has a live profile to close.|

runners_data.name: Eastmore
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins is a key booking; Eastmore's record is almost absurdly consistent on Good ground (sim-going: 14/15, 1W7P) with four seconds from his last five — prominent style matches the anticipated race shape and the Byrnes yard connection with Youlita could mean a tactical pairing.|

runners_data.name: Emesteraye
runners_data.note: Danny Gilligan partners this hold-up type who is 3 from 4 recorded runs on Good (3/17f/GOO is best); moderate trainer strike rate (4/24 T14) and the form string (608-3) offers limited encouragement in a competitive field.|

runners_data.name: Regards To Rose
runners_data.note: Won on Good at 16f last time (1/16f/GOO) and has placed at a variety of distances and going types; prominent style suits this shape well and trainer McCarthy (1/12 T14) has the yard active — tongue-tie worn and G B Noonan does the steering.|

runners_data.name: Northern Ruler
runners_data.note: Consistently poor recent form (6th, 12th, 17th) and a true hold-up horse whose best ground sim record is weak (0W2P from 15); pushed forward on the map because the field is deep in hold-up types, but his actual race position will be towards the rear where his form does not inspire.|

runners_data.name: Inchidaly Copper
runners_data.note: Solid Limerick course form over Good (3/20f/GOO, 3/21f/GOO, 1/23f/GOO) but off 242 days and with a new stable (T14: 0/0); his natural prominent style cannot be accommodated in this front-heavy field and Luke Burke Ott (7) claims — fitness after eight months is the overriding concern, though the Good-ground course record is worth noting.|

races.paceDynamic: Youlita is the one confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival to press her from the outset on Good ground at Limerick, she is set to control this from the front at a sustainable, measured tempo. Dairy Force and Harpy Eagle are natural prominent types who will look to sit just off the leader, while Eastmore and Regards To Rose add further bodies to the forward ranks, meaning the early order ahead of the hurdles will be genuinely competitive. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate at their natural positions — Inchidaly Copper is a genuine prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that berth, and Northern Ruler is a true hold-up horse pushed further forward on the map than he will actually race. A Youlita-led, controlled pace on Good ground over 2m½f sets up best for horses who can travel prominently in a rhythm and finish strongly from mid-to-close range — prominent racers with Good-ground course form and the ability to pick up over the final two hurdles are the profile to favour.

scenarios.body: If Youlita dictates an uncontested, even gallop and a prominent hold-on type picks up cleanly from the second-last.

scenarios.trigger: If Youlita's controlled lead becomes a full front-running exercise and the pace stays honest enough to drain closers.
scenarios.body: If Youlita's controlled lead becomes a full front-running exercise and the pace stays honest enough to drain closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly strong early and the race develops into a truly run contest with a strong closing burst.
scenarios.body: If the pace is unexpectedly strong early and the race develops into a truly run contest with a strong closing burst.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Late
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches behind Youlita, hurdle errors disrupt the order and a rough-and-tumble finish rewards a lucky position.
scenarios.body: If the field bunches behind Youlita, hurdle errors disrupt the order and a rough-and-tumble finish rewards a lucky position.

watchPoints.text: Eastmore has finished placed in 8 of his last 15 runs on Good ground — if Danny Mullins slots him behind Youlita from the outset, he is positioned exactly where this race shape rewards and could be the hardest horse to pass late.

Youlita is the sole pace-setter and if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, Byrnes could be celebrating a second winner in the race — watch how quickly she establishes her lead after the tapes rise.

Dairy Force with Jack Kennedy carries the biggest jockey upgrade in the field — if Elliott has this horse cherry-ripe after 48 days off, the prominent position and Good-ground placed form (2/17f/GOO) make him dangerous in the expected shape.

Inchidaly Copper is 242 days off the track with a brand-new trainer entry (T14: 0/0) — if he arrives fit, his Limerick Good-ground record is the best in the field, but the layoff makes him a significant unknown and early market moves should be monitored.

Silly Mongoose won at Limerick on Good just 17 days ago and is clearly at peak fitness — if the early pace is stronger than expected, his hold-up style could produce a late challenge that catches the eye even if he falls short.

races.name: Kevin McManus Bookmaker Grimes Hurdle (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: Jesse Evans
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with four wins in similar Good-ground conditions and a big course-and-distance profile (15/15 sim-going entries, 4 wins); Noel Meade sends him in lightly on 31 days' rest, he wears headgear, and his prominent style means he should be ideally placed throughout — form of 225-31 shows consistency at the highest level.

runners_data.name: Bowensonfire
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott's powerful yard (10 from 94 in 14 days); returning after 87 days off which is a flag, but his Good-ground form is solid (1 win at this level) and a prominent style means he will sit close enough to pounce; the freshness risk is real given only 7/15 similar-going runs place.

runners_data.name: Daddy Long Legs
runners_data.note: Paul Townend partners the confirmed front-runner for Mullins, whose style-fit score of 0.92 flags this as slightly out of his natural range — he has raced more freely and over shorter in recent outings; on Good he has winning form over this trip and a controlled, uncontested lead is the most likely outcome, making him the axis around which this race turns.

runners_data.name: King Of Kingsfield
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type (hg: tp) who needs the pace set in front to be strong enough to close — his two best Going-matched runs both came on Good or better, including a win over 18f; Josh Williamson rides for Elliott, and 82 days since his last run (a string of poor efforts: 31P66) raises a form concern before expecting a revival.

runners_data.name: Run For Oscar
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins rides for C Byrnes, who has just one runner from eight in 14 days — low-volume operation; 259 days off is a major stamina and fitness unknown, and while his Good-ground form shows consistent placed efforts (2/22f, 4/18f), asking him to run a big race first time out after nearly nine months is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Barbizon
runners_data.note: Elliott's four-year-old carries the lightest OR in the field (128) and is a natural front-runner by inclination — held in midfield on this map because the prominent positions are overcrowded; his recent form (1460-) shows a sharp decline after a promising debut win, and at 114 days since last seen, he needs to show he retains that early ability on Good ground at Grade 3 level.

runners_data.name: Queenofthelodge
runners_data.note: Simon Curling's mare is instinctively prominent but ends up mapped back due to race shape congestion; her form of 157-44 shows she has competed off higher marks and she does handle Good (1 win over 20f), though 37 days between runs and a career-high weight of 148lbs are both mild checks against a big run here.

races.paceDynamic: Daddy Long Legs is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a seven-runner field, Paul Townend can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Limerick over 2m½f. Jesse Evans and Bowensonfire are both prominent-inclined and will track close to the pace, ensuring Daddy Long Legs is not allowed to stride entirely alone but is equally unlikely to be seriously pressured into fractions that destroy the field. King Of Kingsfield and Run For Oscar sit in rear as genuine hold-up types, needing a strong enough pace to produce a meaningful closing effort — but with only one true front-runner setting what figures to be a sensible tempo, that gap may not be generated. The field contains more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Barbizon and Queenofthelodge are natural prominent racers but, with Daddy Long Legs, Jesse Evans and Bowensonfire already occupying that ground, both are likely to end up further back than their instincts prefer — meaning neither should be treated as a true hold-up threat. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can travel close to a measured pace and quicken from a position of comfort, rewarding the prominent-to-leading profile above all others.

scenarios.body: If Daddy Long Legs dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and Townend retains control throughout, dictating every surge.

scenarios.body: If Daddy Long Legs sets just enough pace to stretch the field but a prominent tracker produces a sharper turn-of-foot from the penultimate flight.

scenarios.label: C

scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than it appears and King Of Kingsfield or Run For Oscar get the gap they need to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than it appears and King Of Kingsfield or Run For Oscar get the gap they need to finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Midfield Types Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Daddy Long Legs makes a serious jumping error early or the pace collapses and the race becomes a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Daddy Long Legs makes a serious jumping error early or the pace collapses and the race becomes a sprint finish from the home turn.

watchPoints.text: Daddy Long Legs (Townend/Mullins) — if he flukes a gap at the head of affairs and is never seriously challenged for the lead, the race could be over turning for home; watch whether any prominent runner applies pressure to his early sectionals.

Bowensonfire — returning after 87 days off for Gordon Elliott; watch his paddock condition and how keenly he travels in the early stages, as a fresh horse running prominently can either lead or capitulate if the gallop lifts.

Run For Oscar — 259 days off is extreme and Danny Mullins will need to manage him carefully; if he jumps poorly or is outpaced early, he has no realistic route back into the race from a hold-up position on a track where the pace looks modest.

Barbizon and Queenofthelodge — both natural prominent types squeezed out of their preferred position by the race shape; watch where they actually settle at the first — if they do push forward into prominent ground the race shape changes and Daddy Long Legs faces more company than the single front-runner map suggests.

Jesse Evans — his sim-going record of 15/15 entries on Good-type going with four wins stands out as the most consistent going-matched profile in this field; watch whether Sam Ewing positions him close enough to Daddy Long Legs to mount a direct challenge at the second-last.

races.name: Joe Walsh Flooring Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bhean Saibhre
runners_data.note: Natural prominent type who drops back to a trip (2m4f) on which she has placed twice on Good ground; Peter Smithers (7lb claimer) is a factor on weight, and the sim-going record of 10 from 15 on Good underlines surface suitability — one to respect from the front end.

runners_data.name: Cocovic
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who is the one horse mapped as the true pacesetter here, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a reminder he has raced prominently when not leading before; controls the race shape entirely, 35 days fresh, but no wins in 7 on similar going tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Desert Cave
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up horse for Ian Donoghue's yard who has shown 1 win and 2 places from 15 runs on Good going, but his last five finishes include four finishes outside the top five; 48 days off, dropping back from 22f may not be ideal.

runners_data.name: Global Skies
runners_data.note: Genuinely strong recent form — 1st and 2nd in last two runs both on Good at 20f — makes him the most interesting hold-up type in the field; Danny Gilligan partners a horse whose sim-going record (7 from 15) is acceptable and trip looks ideal.

runners_data.name: Qaasid
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won on Soft last time (20f) and has reasonable Good-ground placed form, though his sim-going shows no wins and no places from 11 Good-ground runs, which is a clear flag; his trainer T14 of 2/31 suggests reasonable recent activity.

runners_data.name: The First Turn
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who is 5-from-5 on similar going in the sim-going filter with 1 win and 1 place — that number stands out in this field; returns to 16f minimum but has two wins at that trip on Good already, and Phillip Enright in the saddle adds experience.

runners_data.name: General Clermont
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old prominent type with a remarkably consistent sim-going record (14 from 15 on Good) and six places in those runs with no wins; D E Fitzgerald's 10-year-old will be competitive but may be hard to win with.

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: Hasn't run for 269 days — that layoff is the dominant concern — but Mr Finn Tegetmeier (7lb claimer) takes off weight for Noel Meade's youngster who was 1-3-3 in last three runs, all on Good ground over suitable trips; the freshness angle cuts both ways.

runners_data.name: Warm In Gorey
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has been placed in three of five recent runs on Good going, though his career Going record of 0 wins from 12 on Good is a factual concern; blinkers applied, Simon Torrens rides, and trainer T14 of 2/24 shows active form.

runners_data.name: The Vegas Raider
runners_data.note: 437 days off the track is the overwhelming concern before anything else; by nature a prominent racer, he is positioned in midfield here only because the front-end slots are congested, and the STYLE_FIT flag further tempers expectations on return.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Paradise
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Paul Nolan returning after 47 days; has only four sim-going runs on record (3 from 4 on Good) and none showed a win or place — the statistical base is thin; age 5 gives scope but recent form shows a 16th and a pull-up.

runners_data.name: Pure Logic
runners_data.note: A front-end horse by nature who ends up in midfield because this field is loaded with prominent types — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) reflects that displacement; his actual Going record shows 8 from 9 on Good but zero wins and four places, useful form without a winning punch.

runners_data.name: Committee Meeting
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse who is mapped to midfield here due to overcrowding at the rear — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) captures the friction; recent form is poor (P, 12th, 8th) and blinkers are applied again, suggesting connections are searching for answers.

runners_data.name: Friar Hogan
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish and a true hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map for the same congestion reason; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) applies, and the recent form string of 060-0C with zero sim-going wins or places on Good makes this a difficult profile to support.

runners_data.name: Cullenwaine
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer who has placed 2nd-2nd-2nd-5th in recent Good-ground runs at 22f — clearly loves the trip and going — but sits in midfield on the map because this field simply cannot accommodate all the prominent types; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects that he may not get his favoured berth, which would reduce his chance.

races.paceDynamic: Cocovic is the one confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner field and, with the pace map showing no genuine rival willing to press from the front, he is likely to dictate at a measured, sustainable gallop over the 2m4f trip on Good ground at Limerick. That controlled tempo will compress the field through the middle stages and make it genuinely difficult for hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need in the straight. The sustainable pace benefits prominent racers who can travel close to Cocovic without burning fuel, track him into the final bend, and pick up sharply — Bhean Saibhre, Qaasid, General Clermont and Warm In Gorey are the natural beneficiaries. The field carries a significant surplus of prominent types: The Vegas Raider, Pure Logic and Cullenwaine are all genuine front-end or close-up horses by nature who are mapped to midfield only because the prominent slots are oversubscribed — Cocovic and Bhean Saibhre are most likely to actually secure the lead positions, with Qaasid and General Clermont disputing the next slots.

watchPoints.text: Cocovic controls the pace entirely — if he gets a clean lead and bowls along unchallenged, the whole field's fate depends on whether they can overhaul him in the straight; watch for any early pressure from Cullenwaine or Pure Logic trying to push up and disrupt that dominance.
The Vegas Raider returns after 437 days off: watch for signs of rustiness in the early stages or a sluggish jump that puts him out of contention before the race has shaped up.

Mickey Cohen's 269-day absence means his fitness is unproven — if Noel Meade has him wound up he could be significant, but watch carefully in the paddock and early exchanges for any sign of ring-rustiness.

Global Skies has won and placed in his last two on identical going and trip — watch how Danny Gilligan places him through the field, as this horse has the profile to produce a late challenge if the pace compresses the front-runners.

With three or four natural prominent types (The Vegas Raider, Pure Logic, Cullenwaine, Bhean Saibhre) all seeking to race close to Cocovic, watch the first three hurdles for jostling and potential interference that could unsettle runners and alter the race shape entirely.

races.name: Munster Suite At Limerick Races Handicap Hurdle (0-100) (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Charlie's Dilemma
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner here; McConnell's seven-year-old has the licence to control and his Good-ground figures at similar trips (sim-going 10 runs, 0W5P) suggest he is consistent but vulnerable if opponents arrive fresh at the last — the STYLE_FIT flag is irrelevant since he IS the pace.|

runners_data.name: Illtakehimmyself
runners_data.note: McNamara's five-year-old has finished second on consecutive outings and clearly handles Good ground, climbing the trip to 2m6½f here; placed four times from seven runs on similar going and his prominent style suits an uncontested gallop perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Any Chance
runners_data.note: Unknown style makes him hard to place tactically; two runs on Good going produced a sixth and a twelfth and this is the longest trip he has faced, so stamina and trip are both queries.|

runners_data.name: Stretchemout
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 232 days off, which is the longest layoff in the field; won at 21f on Good ground and has course experience, but the absence and the wait-and-pounce style are both negatives in this steady-pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: Sallap
runners_data.note: Dual winner on Good ground and clearly acts on this surface; the fades-in-finish tag is a concern over 2m6½f but has shown front-running ability before and if he travels well in midfield he could be involved despite that stamina question.|

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Placed at 22f on Good ground and handles this surface, but three jumps-related exits (U, F, F) in recent form create jumping reliability concern; hold-up style in a sustainable pace is not ideal.|

runners_data.name: Le Fanu
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old who won last time at 20f on Good ground and goes on this surface comfortably; prominent style is perfectly suited to the predicted race shape and the Brendan Walsh yard is operating at a solid level.|

runners_data.name: Ocean Murphy
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with only one run on Good ground in his last five, returning after 95 days; the hold-up profile and limited Good-ground evidence make him a spectator in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Stumblin In
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose 13 runs on Good going have produced one win and two places, so he handles the surface, but the style does not suit an uncontested gallop over this trip and the fades tag adds further doubt.|

runners_data.name: Friends Of Barry
runners_data.note: Went close (2nd) last time at 22f on Good ground and clearly acts on it; tagged as fading late which is a real concern stepped up to 2m6½f, but Philip Enright is a capable handler of mid-pack finishers.|

runners_data.name: Whatafoolbelieves
runners_data.note: McConnell runner whose true home is at the rear of the field; the redistribution to midfield reflects the overcrowded hold-up division, and the fades-in-finish flag combined with a STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90 makes him difficult to fancy in this shape.|

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes over on a nine-year-old who is 14/15 on Good ground and has the right prominent style for this pace; the senior partner's 1W4P sim-going record shows he can hit the frame and the Eoin Doyle-Slevin combination warrants respect.|

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Gold
runners_data.note: Ran second at 24f on Good ground two starts ago showing he stays this trip; a true hold-up horse who has been shifted to midfield on the map, though with Good-ground experience and Danny Mullins aboard he is the redistributed type most capable of creeping into contention.|

runners_data.name: Can't Catch Molly
runners_data.note: Winless in five starts and 0/5 on Good ground; placed into midfield from the hold-up division, yet form figures of 00006 offer little encouragement regardless of where she races in the field.|

runners_data.name: Liss Eile
runners_data.note: Has finished fourth at 16f on Good ground and the handicapper has dropped her to OR 81; a natural hold-up horse placed into midfield on the map, her best form has come over shorter trips than today's 2m6½f.|

runners_data.name: Stone Rulya
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with 0W0P in eight starts on similar going and four consecutive finishes of 8-10-11-10; holds the redistribution flag and a fades-in-finish warning — difficult to make a case for him in any scenario.|

runners_data.name: Mollys Dolly
runners_data.note: Trainer David O'Brien sends out a 6-year-old with a consistent record at 20f on Good ground (6-5) but a tell-tale fades-in-finish pattern; the redistribution from rear to midfield means she is unlikely to get her natural stalking position.|

runners_data.name: Tennesse Boy
runners_data.note: Returned from a long absence (245 days including a P last time) and ran second at 26f on Good ground two starts ago, suggesting the stamina is there; however, the hold-up redistribution, fades-in-finish flag and that problematic jumping record (P last run) make him hard to trust.|

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Unattached jockey entry here; prominent style suits the pace map and he has 1W7P from 15 similar-going starts, showing remarkable consistency — trainer John Patrick Ryan at 2/29 over 14 days is a live flag, and 8/26f on Good ground is recent and relevant.|

races.paceDynamic: Charlie's Dilemma is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and should control matters from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 2m6½f trip on Good ground at Limerick. Illtakehimmyself, Le Fanu, U Asking Me and Smallcraftwarning will press prominently behind, creating an organised but not truly pressured tempo that is unlikely to shred the field early. With no rival likely to seriously challenge Charlie's Dilemma for the lead, the pace will be honest but measured, meaning the race will be run to suit horses who can travel close to the pace and produce a finish rather than those who need a truly gruelling test to deliver from deep. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and close-up travellers who can sustain their effort from the home turn; genuine hold-up horses are disadvantaged here because the sustainable pace will not create the bunching and late-race carnage they need to deliver a finishing kick. Several runners — including Stone Rulya, Whatafoolbelieves, Liss Eile, Ballinaboola Gold, Can't Catch Molly, Mollys Dolly and Tennesse Boy — are true hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield simply because this field is too hold-up heavy for them all to race at the rear; of those, Stone Rulya and Ballinaboola Gold are best placed to creep closer than their natural style, but Le Fanu, Illtakehimmyself and U Asking Me are the ones most likely to actually secure and maintain a prominent position throughout.

watchPoints.text: Charlie's Dilemma is the only genuine pace-setter in a 19-runner field — watch whether Illtakehimmyself or Le Fanu push up to dispute early; if they do, the gallop increases and the race flips entirely away from a front-runner's race.|

Stretchemout returns from 232 days off with hold-up tendencies in a race shape that does not suit wait-and-pounce — he is the most likely runner to need a strong pace that will probably never materialise and could be a false favourite.|

U Asking Me is 14/15 on Good ground and J J Slevin takes over — this combo looks dangerously straightforward on paper, but nine-year-old legs and a P last time (albeit at a shorter trip) means jumping errors late are a genuine risk.|

Ballinaboola Gold and Stone Rulya are both redistributed hold-up horses who will not get their natural position; if any of them drift wide or cause interference on the home turn in a 19-runner field, they could take out a prominent contender.|

Sallap's fades-in-finish flag becomes critical at 2m6½f — watch whether Michael Kenneally (5lb claimer) attempts to inject early pace to get her into a better jumping rhythm, which would inadvertently raise the early tempo and change the race shape.|

races.name: Munster Suite At Limerick Races Handicap Hurdle (0-100)

runners_data.name: Mickey Hulie
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here; Danny Mullins can dictate terms unchallenged, but at 6yo running over 2m6½f on Good — a step up in trip — stamina questions remain after a 35-day break, and the STYLE_FIT flag notes it is effectively racing out of its most comfortable role.|

runners_data.name: Ishan
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent type with five recent runs on Good going but zero wins or places on that surface (0W0P in 15 sim-going runs); 27 days since last run, and the form string 359-80 offers little encouragement in a competitive 0-100 field.|

runners_data.name: Fire Coral
runners_data.note: Two recent wins on Good at similar distances (22f and 24f) in last five starts give it a strong profile for this trip and surface; prominent style suits a controlled-pace scenario perfectly, and the tongue-tie is worn routinely — this profile fits the dominant race shape well.|

runners_data.name: The Rebel County
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type (cheekpieces) who has placed on Good ground and over similar trips, but a 5lb claimer (Alan O'Sullivan) navigating a 19-runner field from the rear is a significant ask; 19 days since last run, and recent finishing positions (3,4,4) show consistency without a win.|

runners_data.name: Technology
runners_data.note: Prominent traveller for Alan King making his first run in 269 days — the layoff is a serious flag — but two recent placings at 24f on Good suggest the style and stamina profile fit well if fitness is retained; bears watching early to gauge how fresh he is.|

runners_data.name: Ellies Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent type who fell last time out (F in form string) which may have left a physical or mental mark; has won at shorter trips on Soft and has limited Good-going form (0W0P in 5 runs), so the surface is not conclusively in its favour at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Gortmore Lady
runners_data.note: True hold-up mare (4 places from 14 similar-going runs, 0 wins) who will need the prominent pack to capitulate; trainer Ciaran Murphy had one runner in the last 20 days which returned a winner (1/20 T14), but from the back in a 19-runner controlled-pace race, the task is steep.|

runners_data.name: Whatyouwant
runners_data.note: Won at 25f on Good so the distance/surface combination is proven; off 279 days, which is a major concern, and the form string 0061P- shows inconsistency — cheekpieces worn, which adds a behavioural variable on return from a near-nine-month absence.|

runners_data.name: Knocknagoran Lady
runners_data.note: Placed twice in recent history at 24f on Good, prominent in running style, and the tongue-tie plus visor combination suggests connections are trying to sharpen her up; jockey Daniel King and trainer Cian Hughes are a quiet partnership but the form trajectory (6th last time) is flat.|

runners_data.name: Ballyredinkingston
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has struggled to fire recently (000B-6 form) with only one place from 11 similar-going runs; the 5lb claimer (Michael Kenneally) will need to find daylight in a 19-runner field from the rear, and a 17-day turnaround after a pulled-up run is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Western Opera
runners_data.note: Has won at 22f on Good (placed at 22f too) so the distance and surface are within range, but the last run was a pull-up and the form 026-P5 is uninspiring; genuine hold-up type who needs a genuine gallop to close into — unlikely to get it here.|

runners_data.name: Hob's Angel
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old who has won and placed on Good ground at 20f recently (form: 606-12), but the step up to 2m6½f is new territory; prominent style suits this shape, and the 5lb claimer Josh Williamson is a small negative weight in a tight finish.|

runners_data.name: Phildante
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with headgear (tongue-tie and cheekpieces) who has consistently finished in mid-division (4th, 6th, 6th) without threatening; 23 days since last run is fine, but the profile is a non-factor unless the pace genuinely collapses.|

runners_data.name: Lady Aquarelle
runners_data.note: The form note flags a tendency to fade late, which is a critical warning for a horse pushed into a midfield map position; naturally a hold-up type who has never won or placed on similar going in 5 attempts (0W0P), and the redistribution compounds an already limited profile.|

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: Runs prominently by nature but the map places it in midfield because there are simply too many prominent types here; form reads PP8-0P — three pulls-up or unfinished runs in recent history — making this a significant risk horse regardless of where it races.|

runners_data.name: Annie Questions
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up runner who also carries a late-fade flag — a dangerous combination in a race likely to be run at a controlled pace; though placed once in 11 similar-going runs, the redistribution to midfield means it is unlikely to be in its comfort zone throughout.|

runners_data.name: Captain Kate
runners_data.note: Has placed at 25f and 26f on Good, so the distance and surface are not concerns, but 231 days off the track is a serious fitness flag; naturally races from hold-up but is mapped to midfield — the long layoff and positional compromise make this very hard to support.|

runners_data.name: Tuff Days
runners_data.note: A prominent runner by nature but squeezed to a midfield mapping because there is no room at the head of affairs; nine-year-old with 0 wins from 15 similar-going runs (0W0P), and the form 6U2-60 shows no win since — the style displacement hurts an already moderate recent profile.|

runners_data.name: Another Glendaars
runners_data.note: No jockey listed which is an immediate query; hold-up type who has finished 4th-7th in all five recent runs (sim-going: 5 runs), never won or placed on similar going, and trainer C Byrnes has one winner from eight in the last 14 days — consistent without threatening.|

races.paceDynamic: Mickey Hulie is the only confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner field and, crucially, faces no serious pressure for the lead — the next-most-naturally prominent horses (Fire Coral, Ishan, Technology, Ellies Rock) are all comfortable stalking types rather than pace-pressers, meaning Mickey Hulie should dictate at whatever tempo Danny Mullins chooses over 2m6½f on Good ground. With no rival likely to force a hot early pace, the race will be run at a controlled, even gallop that compresses the field and reduces the advantage of horses attempting to come from the back, leaving those tracking the leader in the prime position. Several horses labelled as prominent or hold-up types — Tuff Days, Set The Tone, Lady Aquarelle, Annie Questions and Captain Kate — cannot all secure their preferred positions in a 19-runner field, meaning the midfield will be congested and truly deep closers will struggle to thread through in time. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-mid-pack stalkers who can sit within a few lengths of Mickey Hulie and pounce from a handy position off the final bend, with pure hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Mickey Hulie has no pacemaker rival to worry about but watch the opening half-mile closely — if Danny Mullins elects to dawdle dangerously, the entire field could compress and the prominent stalkers (Fire Coral, Technology) will be camped on his quarters from an early stage.|

Technology has been off the track for 269 days; watch the paddock and early racing — if he travels strongly it signals genuine fitness, but a horse returning from nine months absent in a 19-runner field over 2m6½f is a significant each-way risk if he blows up.|

Set The Tone has pulled up or was unfinished in three of its last five starts — in a 19-runner hurdle field this represents a jumping and safety concern, particularly in the first half of the race where the field will be tightly grouped.|

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Lady Aquarelle, Annie Questions, Captain Kate, Ballyredinkingston) will all be jostling for midfield positions they are not naturally comfortable in — watch for traffic problems turning out of the back straight as these horses attempt to find racing room.|

Whatyouwant and Captain Kate both return from layoffs exceeding 230 days — monitor their pre-race market moves; any significant support for either would indicate stable confidence that fitness has been maintained, which would materially shift their scenario relevance.|
